simple: a small operating system for microcontrollers that tries to look like Unix to the programs on it.
analogy: the rule in Lina's body that decides which job gets her attention first.
precise: an open-source real-time operating system of the Apache Software Foundation that emphasises compliance with standards (POSIX and ANSI C) and a small footprint, and scales across microcontroller families; it is the operating system PX4 uses on most flight-controller boards.
source: D2 of F10-20 (Apache NuttX project (Apache Software Foundation), "NuttX Documentation": introduction and features, tasks and pthreads, scheduling, build modes (flat, protected, kernel), NSH, the simulator (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D1 of F10-20 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide", development sections on the architectural overview, NuttX, the platform layer and modules (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two names for a job the scheduler runs; a task is started on its own, a thread belongs to a task.
analogy: a helper with their own job card, and a second pair of hands working for the same helper.
precise: in NuttX a task is a schedulable entity with its own stack and its own resources (such as open files), created by NuttX's task-creation interface; a pthread is created by a task with pthread_create and shares its parent task's resources; both are scheduled by the same priority-based scheduler. The exact API names and resource-sharing rules are in the unverified box of Layer 3.
source: D2 of F10-20 (Apache NuttX project (Apache Software Foundation), "NuttX Documentation": introduction and features, tasks and pthreads, scheduling, build modes (flat, protected, kernel), NSH, the simulator (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the rule "the most urgent job runs, and keeps running until it waits or someone more urgent arrives".
analogy: the balance reflex: nothing interrupts it except something even more urgent.
precise: the POSIX first-in-first-out real-time scheduling policy: fixed priorities, preemption by higher priorities, and no time slicing among equal priorities.
source: D3 of F10-20 (The Open Group and IEEE, "The Open Group Base Specifications" (IEEE Std 1003.1, POSIX.1): pthread_create, pthread_attr_setinheritsched, sched_get_priority_max, scheduling policies, clock_nanosleep, mq_open, mq_send, mq_receive, sem_post (tier 1)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: "wake me at 10:00:04", not "wake me in 4 seconds".
analogy: stepping on the beat of music, not counting four steps after you last finished one.
precise: sleeping until a point on a clock (clock_nanosleep with TIMER_ABSTIME), so that the next release is the previous release plus the period, independent of how late the task woke or how long it worked.
source: D3 of F10-20 (The Open Group and IEEE, "The Open Group Base Specifications" (IEEE Std 1003.1, POSIX.1): pthread_create, pthread_attr_setinheritsched, sched_get_priority_max, scheduling policies, clock_nanosleep, mq_open, mq_send, mq_receive, sem_post (tier 1)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F10-20 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (posix_rate.log))

simple: how much later than planned a periodic task actually starts.
analogy: how far off the beat Lina's step lands.
precise: the time from a job's planned release to the moment the task observes it is running; its worst value bounds the start of every job and adds to the response time.
source: D4 of F10-20 (Giorgio Buttazzo, "Hard Real-Time Computing Systems: Predictable Scheduling Algorithms and Applications" (tier 3): release, lateness, response time, blocking and priority inversion) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a mailbox of fixed-size messages between tasks.
analogy: a small tray where one helper puts notes and another takes them, in order.
precise: a kernel object opened by name with mq_open, holding up to mq_maxmsg messages of at most mq_msgsize bytes; mq_send blocks when it is full and mq_receive blocks when it is empty (unless non-blocking mode is set).
source: D3 of F10-20 (The Open Group and IEEE, "The Open Group Base Specifications" (IEEE Std 1003.1, POSIX.1): pthread_create, pthread_attr_setinheritsched, sched_get_priority_max, scheduling policies, clock_nanosleep, mq_open, mq_send, mq_receive, sem_post (tier 1)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: in a flat build every task can write anywhere in memory; in a protected build the hardware stops writes outside allowed areas.
analogy: everyone carrying drinks on one shared tray, versus each helper with their own tray.
precise: NuttX build configurations that differ in memory protection: the flat build links the kernel and all applications into one address space with no protection; the protected build uses the microcontroller's memory protection unit (MPU) to separate kernel and user parts; a kernel build uses an MMU and separate address spaces. Build-mode names and requirements are in the unverified box.
source: D2 of F10-20 (Apache NuttX project (Apache Software Foundation), "NuttX Documentation": introduction and features, tasks and pthreads, scheduling, build modes (flat, protected, kernel), NSH, the simulator (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the text command line of NuttX.
analogy: a walkie-talkie into Lina's head: you can ask what each part of her is doing.
precise: the NuttShell, NuttX's shell application, which runs commands typed on a console and from start-up scripts; PX4 uses it as the console on its flight controllers.
source: D2 of F10-20 (Apache NuttX project (Apache Software Foundation), "NuttX Documentation": introduction and features, tasks and pthreads, scheduling, build modes (flat, protected, kernel), NSH, the simulator (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D1 of F10-20 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide", development sections on the architectural overview, NuttX, the platform layer and modules (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one self-contained part of the flight software, such as a sensor driver, the estimator or a controller.
analogy: one member of Lina's team with a clear role.
precise: a unit of PX4 software that is built, started, stopped and queried on its own (through a shell command with sub-commands such as start, stop and status) and that communicates with other modules only through uORB topics.
source: D1 of F10-21 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": architectural overview, modules and commands reference, work queues, uORB (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one thread that runs many small jobs, one after another.
analogy: one helper working down a list of quick jobs, in order.
precise: in PX4, a thread with a fixed priority and its own stack that runs the work items scheduled on it in first-in, first-out order, each to completion; several work queues exist with different priorities, so that urgent work is not delayed by less urgent work.
source: D1 of F10-21 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": architectural overview, modules and commands reference, work queues, uORB (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small job that is put on a work queue whenever it is due.
analogy: one quick job on a helper's list ("refill glass 3").
precise: an object with a run function that is scheduled on a particular work queue, either on a fixed interval or when a uORB topic it watches is published; while it is already waiting in the queue, a new request does not queue it a second time.
source: D1 of F10-21 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": architectural overview, modules and commands reference, work queues, uORB (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F10-21 (R1 — lab run of Listings 1 and 2 (wq_sim.log))

simple: once a job starts on a list, the helper finishes it before taking the next.
analogy: Tomás does not stop washing cups halfway to refill a glass.
precise: items on one work queue do not preempt each other; an item can only be preempted by threads of higher priority (other work queues, tasks, interrupts). Therefore an item can be blocked by any item of its own queue that is already running or queued ahead of it.
source: D1 of F10-21 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": architectural overview, modules and commands reference, work queues, uORB (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D4 of F10-21 (Giorgio Buttazzo, "Hard Real-Time Computing Systems: Predictable Scheduling Algorithms and Applications"; Alan Burns and Andy Wellings, "Real-Time Systems and Programming Languages" (tier 3): response-time analysis with blocking for non-preemptive sections. Titles only — not opened during this build (dossier gate G1 open)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the extra wait caused by a less urgent job that is in the way and cannot be interrupted.
analogy: the ten minutes of cup washing in front of "refill glass 3".
precise: in response-time analysis, the term B added to a job's response time for non-preemptible work of equal or lower urgency that can delay it; for a work item, the longest execution time among the other items of its own queue that can be ahead of it.
source: D4 of F10-21 (Giorgio Buttazzo, "Hard Real-Time Computing Systems: Predictable Scheduling Algorithms and Applications"; Alan Burns and Andy Wellings, "Real-Time Systems and Programming Languages" (tier 3): response-time analysis with blocking for non-preemptive sections. Titles only — not opened during this build (dossier gate G1 open)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: asking for a job that is already on the list does not add it twice.
analogy: "glass 3 is empty" shouted twice is still one refill.
precise: in this chapter's model (and, by the PX4 documentation's description, in PX4's work queues), scheduling an item that is already queued or running does not create a second entry; the request is lost as a separate run, which shows up as fewer runs than releases.
source: R1 of F10-21 (R1 — lab run of Listings 1 and 2 (wq_sim.log)); D1 of F10-21 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": architectural overview, modules and commands reference, work queues, uORB (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: PX4 modules that decide the flight mode and arming, plan where to go, and record the flight.
analogy: the team leader, the route planner, and Kwame writing the day's notes.
precise: PX4 modules described in the PX4 Autopilot User Guide: the commander handles vehicle state, arming and failsafes; the navigator executes missions and automatic modes; the logger writes selected uORB topics to a ULog file (F10-25).
source: D1 of F10-21 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": architectural overview, modules and commands reference, work queues, uORB (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: PX4's notice board: modules post data there and read data from there.
analogy: the board by the kitchen door.
precise: PX4's asynchronous publish/subscribe messaging layer for communication between modules (and threads) inside one flight-stack instance; data is exchanged as fixed-size message structs on named topics.
source: D1 of F10-22 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "uORB Messaging" and related pages (message definitions, multi-instance topics, queue length, scheduling on publication, bridges to ROS 2) (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one named kind of message, like "attitude" or "battery status".
analogy: one labelled space on the board.
precise: a named channel with exactly one message type, defined in a message definition file from which PX4's build generates a C++ struct; every message carries a timestamp. The ROS 2 topic of F9-37 is the same idea across processes and machines.
source: D1 of F10-22 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "uORB Messaging" and related pages (message definitions, multi-instance topics, queue length, scheduling on publication, bridges to ROS 2) (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the writer's handle and the reader's handle for a topic.
analogy: pinning a note; walking past and reading.
precise: a publication writes a new message to the topic without waiting for any reader; a subscription remembers which message it last read, can tell whether a newer one exists ("updated"), and copies it out.
source: D1 of F10-22 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "uORB Messaging" and related pages (message definitions, multi-instance topics, queue length, scheduling on publication, bridges to ROS 2) (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F10-22 (R1 — lab run of Listings 1 and 2 (uorb_demo.log))

simple: how many of the newest messages the topic keeps.
analogy: how many notes fit in one board space before the oldest comes down.
precise: the size of a topic's ring of recent messages; with length 1, a reader sees only the latest message; with length n, a reader that falls fewer than n messages behind can still read every message in order.
source: D1 of F10-22 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "uORB Messaging" and related pages (message definitions, multi-instance topics, queue length, scheduling on publication, bridges to ROS 2) (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F10-22 (R1 — lab run of Listings 1 and 2 (uorb_demo.log))

simple: a running number of how many messages were ever published on a topic.
analogy: the number written on each note: 1, 2, 3…
precise: a monotonically increasing count kept by the topic; a subscription compares its own position with it to decide whether it is up to date and how many messages were overwritten before it read them.
source: R1 of F10-22 (R1 — lab run of Listings 1 and 2 (uorb_demo.log)); D1 of F10-22 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "uORB Messaging" and related pages (message definitions, multi-instance topics, queue length, scheduling on publication, bridges to ROS 2) (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: several copies of the same topic, one per sensor of the same kind.
analogy: two spaces labelled "GPS", numbered 0 and 1.
precise: a topic that can be advertised more than once, each advertisement getting an instance index; subscribers choose the instance (for example the second IMU) and redundancy logic compares instances.
source: D1 of F10-22 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "uORB Messaging" and related pages (message definitions, multi-instance topics, queue length, scheduling on publication, bridges to ROS 2) (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the reader only cares about the newest message.
analogy: Lina reading the newest route note.
precise: a usage in which missing intermediate messages is harmless because each message is a complete state (an attitude, a setpoint); contrast with messages that carry increments (an angle change since the last message), where every message matters.
source: R2 of F10-22 (R2 — run of the forensic model forensic_yaw.cpp (forensic_yaw.log), exit code 0.)

simple: the real flight software runs on a normal computer and a simulator plays the drone and the world.
analogy: rehearsing the walk in the hallway with plastic cups.
precise: a test configuration in which the flight stack is compiled for the host operating system and exchanges sensor data and actuator commands with a physics simulator instead of hardware drivers; PX4 supports SITL with several simulators.
source: D1 of F10-23 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "Building PX4 Software", development environment and toolchain installation, "Simulation" (SITL, HITL, lockstep, supported simulators) (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the real flight controller runs the real firmware, but its sensors are replaced by a simulator.
analogy: the real tray, in the hallway, with a friend shouting the bumps.
precise: a configuration in which the firmware runs on the flight-controller hardware and receives simulated sensor data (and sends actuator outputs) over a link to a simulator on a computer; it tests the firmware on its real processor and operating system without flying (F10-34).
source: D1 of F10-23 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "Building PX4 Software", development environment and toolchain installation, "Simulation" (SITL, HITL, lockstep, supported simulators) (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: simulator and flight software take turns: the simulator waits for the answer before it moves time forward.
analogy: the coach says "step" and waits until you have stepped.
precise: a coupling in which simulated time advances only after the flight stack has processed the current sensor data and returned its actuator outputs, so that the result is independent of how fast either runs in wall-clock time.
source: D1 of F10-23 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "Building PX4 Software", development environment and toolchain installation, "Simulation" (SITL, HITL, lockstep, supported simulators) (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F10-23 (R1 — lab run of Listings 1 and 2 (sitl_lockstep.log))

simple: the name you give the build to say which board and which set of modules you want.
analogy: choosing which tray and which drinks before you start.
precise: a name passed to PX4's top-level build (a Makefile front end that drives CMake) that selects a vendor, a board and a configuration label; a SITL target selects the host platform instead of a board.
source: D1 of F10-23 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "Building PX4 Software", development environment and toolchain installation, "Simulation" (SITL, HITL, lockstep, supported simulators) (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D2 of F10-23 (Kitware, "CMake Documentation" (tier 2): configure and build steps, generators) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the piece of code that translates between the simulator's world and the flight stack's sensor and motor messages.
analogy: the friend who calls out the bumps: if he uses the wrong units, everything goes wrong.
precise: the module or plugin that converts simulator state into the flight stack's sensor topics (with timestamps) and actuator topics into simulator inputs, over a defined protocol; it replaces the hardware drivers in SITL.
source: D1 of F10-23 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "Building PX4 Software", development environment and toolchain installation, "Simulation" (SITL, HITL, lockstep, supported simulators) (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the single file that is written into the flight controller's memory.
analogy: the packed tray, ready to carry.
precise: the linked binary of PX4 and NuttX for one board, packaged with metadata, which a bootloader on the board writes into flash.
source: D1 of F10-23 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "Building PX4 Software", development environment and toolchain installation, "Simulation" (SITL, HITL, lockstep, supported simulators) (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: what happens when a module starts, works, reports and stops.
analogy: the helper arrives, does the job, answers "how is it going?", leaves and clears the table.
precise: the sequence start (allocate, subscribe, register periodic work, read parameters), run (periodic or triggered work), status (print counters and state), stop (cancel work, release subscriptions and memory); PX4 provides base classes that implement the common parts (unverified box).
source: D1 of F10-24 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "Modules & Commands", module template, "uORB Messaging", "Parameters & Configurations", start-up scripts, "First Application Tutorial" (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a job that the system runs again and again at a fixed interval on a work queue.
analogy: "every ten seconds, look at the tray".
precise: a work item (F10-21) registered with an interval; the work queue thread calls its run function when the interval elapses, to completion, then waits for the next one. A work item can instead be triggered by a uORB publication.
source: D1 of F10-24 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "Modules & Commands", module template, "uORB Messaging", "Parameters & Configurations", start-up scripts, "First Application Tutorial" (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F10-24 (R1 — lab run of shell.cpp with shell.in (shell.log))

simple: a named setting of a module that the operator can change without rebuilding.
analogy: "tray limit is now 20°".
precise: a named, typed value stored in the parameter system, with a default, range and description, that a module reads at start and must re-read when the parameter system announces a change; PX4 announces changes on a topic.
source: D1 of F10-24 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "Modules & Commands", module template, "uORB Messaging", "Parameters & Configurations", start-up scripts, "First Application Tutorial" (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the message that says "some setting changed, check yours".
analogy: the "settings changed" notice.
precise: a publication on a dedicated topic each time any parameter changes; a module subscribes to it and, when it sees an update, reloads its parameters. In this course's runtime the topic is parameter_update_model.
source: D1 of F10-24 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "Modules & Commands", module template, "uORB Messaging", "Parameters & Configurations", start-up scripts, "First Application Tutorial" (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F10-24 (R1 — lab run of shell.cpp with shell.in (shell.log))

simple: a shell command that prints the latest message of a topic.
analogy: walking to the notice board and reading one notice.
precise: a tool that subscribes to a topic and prints its fields; PX4 provides one in its shell (unverified box); this course's shell provides listener tilt_status.
source: D1 of F10-24 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "Modules & Commands", module template, "uORB Messaging", "Parameters & Configurations", start-up scripts, "First Application Tutorial" (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: counting the moment something starts, not every moment it lasts.
analogy: counting how often the tray tipped too far, not how many seconds it stayed tipped.
precise: an event recorded on the transition of a condition from false to true; it needs the previous state to be stored.
source: R1 of F10-24 (R1 — lab run of shell.cpp with shell.in (shell.log))

simple: the file format in which PX4 records a flight.
analogy: the film of the afternoon, with the settings written next to it.
precise: PX4's binary log format: a header, then a definitions section (message formats, information key-value pairs, parameters), then a data section (subscriptions, timestamped topic data, logged strings and parameter changes); written by the logger module, typically to the SD card.
source: D1 of F10-25 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "ULog File Format", "Logging", "Flight Log Analysis" (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a log that contains the description of its own records, so a reader needs no other file.
analogy: each film reel starts with a card saying what is on it.
precise: a format in which every record type is defined inside the file (field names, types, order) before records of that type appear; tools decode any topic without knowing the firmware version.
source: D1 of F10-25 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "ULog File Format", "Logging", "Flight Log Analysis" (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F10-25 (R1 — run.sh step flight_sim (flight_sim.log))

simple: the difference between what a sensor says and what the estimator expected it to say.
analogy: the gap between where the spotter marks Lina and where the head spotter thought she was.
precise: y − h(x̂), the measurement minus the measurement predicted from the current state estimate; its covariance S = HPHᵀ + R (F10-14).
source: D3 of F10-25 (Yaakov Bar-Shalom, X. Rong Li and Thiagalingam Kirubarajan, "Estimation with Applications to Tracking and Navigation" (tier 3): innovations, their covariance, validation gates) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a number that says how surprising a measurement is, scaled so that above 1 means "too surprising, reject".
analogy: "that mark is more than four steps away from where I expected; ignore it".
precise: in this course's estimator, innovation² / (gate² · S), with gate = 4 standard deviations: a measurement with ratio > 1 lies outside the gate and is not fused. PX4's estimator logs test ratios defined in a similar spirit (unverified box).
source: R1 of F10-25 (R1 — run.sh step flight_sim (flight_sim.log)); D2 of F10-25 (PX4 project, "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": EKF2 estimator documentation ("Using the ECL EKF" or its successor), estimator tuning and the "Parameter Reference" (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the limit beyond which a measurement is ignored.
analogy: the "four steps" rule.
precise: a threshold on the normalised innovation that protects the estimate from outliers; set too tight it rejects good data, too loose it accepts bad data.
source: D3 of F10-25 (Yaakov Bar-Shalom, X. Rong Li and Thiagalingam Kirubarajan, "Estimation with Applications to Tracking and Navigation" (tier 3): innovations, their covariance, validation gates) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: where a sensor is mounted relative to the point the estimator tracks.
analogy: the flag 15 cm in front of the handle.
precise: the body-frame vector from the estimator's reference point (usually the IMU or centre of gravity) to the sensor; the estimator rotates it by the attitude to predict the sensor's measurement. A wrong lever arm produces an innovation that changes with heading.
source: D2 of F10-25 (PX4 project, "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": EKF2 estimator documentation ("Using the ECL EKF" or its successor), estimator tuning and the "Parameter Reference" (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D3 of F10-25 (Yaakov Bar-Shalom, X. Rong Li and Thiagalingam Kirubarajan, "Estimation with Applications to Tracking and Navigation" (tier 3): innovations, their covariance, validation gates) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a line of text that the flight software writes into the log at a moment in time.
analogy: Mateus's spoken comment on the film: "she turned now".
precise: a log record with a level, a timestamp and text; in PX4, messages that modules print or send to the ground station are also logged.
source: D1 of F10-25 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "ULog File Format", "Logging", "Flight Log Analysis" (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the work that makes the same flight software run on a new flight-controller board.
analogy: learning a new tray for the same walk.
precise: the board-specific code and configuration for a new flight controller: NuttX board support (clock tree, memory map, pin multiplexing, console, storage), PX4 board files (which drivers, modules and sensors, bus and output mapping), a bootloader, and start-up settings; PX4's generic code is not changed.
source: D1 of F10-26 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "Flight Controller Porting Guide", "PX4 Board Configuration", "NuttX Board Porting Guide", "Bootloader", sensor orientation (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); D2 of F10-26 (Apache NuttX project, "NuttX documentation": boards, configuration, custom boards (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the written list of what is connected where on a board.
analogy: Mateus's drawing of the new tray.
precise: the set of definitions that map board functions to processor resources: which pin is which bus signal, chip select, timer channel or LED; which device sits at which chip select or address; which timer drives which output. In PX4 and NuttX it is spread over several C headers and configuration files (unverified box); in this course it is one text file.
source: D1 of F10-26 (PX4 project (Dronecode Foundation), "PX4 Autopilot User Guide": "Flight Controller Porting Guide", "PX4 Board Configuration", "NuttX Board Porting Guide", "Bootloader", sensor orientation (tier 2)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open); R1 of F10-26 (R1 — lab run of board_check.cpp with board_check.in (board_check.log))

simple: the wire that tells one chip on a shared SPI bus "this message is for you".
analogy: calling one person by name in a group.
precise: a per-device line, driven low by the controller during a transfer, that enables one device on an SPI bus; every device on a bus needs its own chip select.
source: D4 of F10-26 (Arm Limited and the processor vendor's reference manual for the chosen microcontroller (tier 1): pin multiplexing, SPI, I2C and timer peripherals; plus each sensor's datasheet for identity registers (AH-21)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a register in a sensor chip that always returns the same identity number.
analogy: asking a cup holder "which size are you?".
precise: a read-only identification register found in many sensor chips, with a fixed value given in the chip's datasheet; drivers read it at probe time to confirm that the expected chip answers. Register name and value differ per chip (AH-21).
source: D4 of F10-26 (Arm Limited and the processor vendor's reference manual for the chosen microcontroller (tier 1): pin multiplexing, SPI, I2C and timer peripherals; plus each sensor's datasheet for identity registers (AH-21)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: outputs that share one hardware timer and so must share one update rate.
analogy: cup holders that are fixed to one plate.
precise: the channels of one timer peripheral share its counter and period; each channel can have its own pulse width but not its own frequency. Outputs on one timer must use the same rate or protocol (F10-10).
